A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaRewriter study. All 17 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison after text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments across five datasets, reward-model ablations, black-box LLM evaluations and conversation-length analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds results for SFT with chain-of-thought in Table 3.

M1.justification: The proposed candidate-generation procedure, retrieval-based ranking assessment, contrastive ranking loss, DeBERTa reward model and Best-of-N inference remain unchanged. The new SFT variant is a comparator, not an AdaRewriter modification.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TopiOCQA, QReCC and TREC CAsT 2019–2021, retaining sparse/dense retrieval, black-box LLM and long-conversation scenarios. Removing the CAsT 2019 column from Table 3 does not remove that dataset from the paper's evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Section 4.4 and Table 3 add SFT with CoT alongside ordinary SFT and DPO. The SFT/DPO comparison on CAsT 2019 disappears with that table column; comparator membership elsewhere is unchanged.

E3.justification: No independent revision to evaluation design is reported: dataset splits, retrieval systems, metrics, candidate budgets and Appendix B training schedules match. The added CoT comparator uses different training targets within the retained comparison setup.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds a limited comparison of ordinary SFT with CoT-augmented SFT, testing whether including reasoning in training labels helps the training-time alternative. The existing context/loss ablations, black-box evaluations, long-conversation analysis and Appendix D case study remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same t-test reporting at p < 0.05 in Tables 1 and 2. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or other uncertainty-reporting procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds SFT-with-CoT scores of 38.1/58.0 for TopiOCQA MRR/R@10 and 57.7 under the CAsT 2020 column labeled R@10. It removes CAsT 2019 entries of 70.0 for SFT, 66.4 for DPO and 71.4 for AdaRewriter. Retained numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation and Equations 1–6, including the ranking loss, retrieval fusion score and inference rule, are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about Best-of-N reformulation, lightweight reward-model selection, black-box applicability and performance across five datasets.

C2.justification: v2 deletes v1 Appendix A.1, which proposed the reward model as an efficient proxy evaluator and discussed potential applications in RAG and hard-negative mining. The remaining mechanism interpretations and limitations concerning latency, candidate budgets and commercial-model evaluation are unchanged.

D1.justification: The code footnote changes from an anonymous 4open.science repository to the named GitHub repository init0xyz/AdaRewriter. Hardware, hyperparameters, implementation instructions and the Table 8 prompt are retained. The PDFs establish revised access instructions, not whether either repository is operational.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of Kostric and Balog's multi-query rewriting and citations to UniConv, a conversational-search tutorial and Wei et al.'s CoT work. It removes WebWalker with the evaluator discussion. The survey's preprint-to-publication update represents the same cited work; core novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Limited edits expand Section 4.4, clarify the LLM4CS description, correct wording and add acknowledgments. Deleting Appendix A.1 renumbers the retained AdaCQR and CDR discussions. Most prose and the overall section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains the SFT-with-CoT row, loses the CAsT 2019 column and adjusts its spacing. Text and appendix material reflow across pages, while Figures 1–4 and the other table designs remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added SFT-with-CoT comparison tests a relevant training-time alternative, and the expanded related work improves contextual coverage. Removing Table 3's CAsT 2019 results reduces the breadth of that comparison and partly offsets these benefits. With the method and remaining evidence stable, the net improvement is limited.
